CEO and board

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Harlow can lift operating margin to about 3.2% by FY2028 by fixing promotions, shrink and delivery pricing instead of cutting store hours across the board
Wages are not the main cause: promotions, shrink and e-commerce explain 87% of the margin fall since FY2023
–	Operating margin fell from 3.37% to 1.02% in two years; store labor explains only 13% of it
An 8% cut in store hours would miss the target and put fresh produce at risk
–	A shrink rise like that of FY2023–25 would erase about half of its $14.5M saving
Promotions are the largest lever, worth 0.7 percentage points of margin
–	Returning to 24% of sales needs cuts only among the 38% of events that lose money
Home delivery lost about $10M in FY2025; the tested pricing keeps the service and saves about $2.5M a year
–	The team's 6.1% margin leaves out delivery costs and counts every online sale as new
Five moves reach about 3.2% by FY2028, and the three that need no capital come first to clear the covenant
–	The 2027 minimum-wage rise, up to $7.3M a year, is the main risk to the plan

The estimate is cautious on four counts
▪	The 8% cut is deeper than the 6% fall in hours that came with the last rise in shrink
▪	The leanest quarter of stores already loses 3.1% of sales to shrink, compared with 2.6% for the chain
▪	Lost sales from checkout waits and stock-outs are not counted, although 44% of customers come for convenience

Two corrections turn the team's profit into a loss
▪	Third-party delivery is counted; the team's 6.1% margin leaves it out because finance books it in fulfillment
